research_rationale:
EO:6615 (1934-02-26) is a single-clause order under section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 exempting Jacob L. Nuber, Chief of the Printing and Binding Section, Bureau of Internal Revenue from compulsory retirement for age and continuing the person in the service 'until February 28, 1935'. The order ends by its own terms on 1935-02-28 (stated date, inclusive; exclusive alternative one day earlier, per the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling on 'until' dates). Later orders in the same person's exemption chain, read in the packet: EO:6974 (1935-02-21); each is recorded as a later event with its own date and quote (owner ruling, 2026-10-21), and none revokes, amends or shortens this order. The machine term lead dated 1933-02-26 is the recited birthday ('who was 70 years of age on February 26, 1933'), not an end; the operative until-date in the command sentence governs. The dossier's machine term leads were read against the text; the operative until-date in the command sentence is the end. @rationale:retirement:statute @rationale:retirement:search @rationale:retirement:inventory

savings.reason: Service performed and compensation earned while the exemption ran are accrued effects of the person's continued employment; the order creates no continuing duty, office or rule after its stated term. A later 'further' exemption of the same person is a new grant under the statute, not a savings clause of this order, and the person's employment after the stated date rests on that later order, not on this one.
